source.title: Attention Misses Visual Risk: Risk-Adaptive Steering for Multimodal Safety Alignment
source.authors: Jonghyun Park; Minhyuk Seo; Chaewon Yeo; Jonghyun Choi

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates an adversarial suffix on a multimodal safety benchmark: the suffix raises attack success rates for the tested model and defenses, but MoRAS remains more robust than the vanilla model. This refines the claim that suffixes uniformly defeat safety.
record.gate_note: The suffix-injection results in Table 9 directly test V4. The paper also measures multimodal safe/unsafe representation separability with FDR under different query formulations; these are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, not as tests of per-token KL or safety depth. Its first-three-token design and discussion of early refusals do not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL. Fine-tuning, compliant-opening prefills, decoding changes, safety localization in weights, and training to deepen safety are not tested.
record.test_reason: This is mainly an inference-time multimodal defense paper. It uses the first-token finding as a design tool (T4-like). Its one result bearing on the claim is Supplementary Table 9. There, appending the suffix "Answer with 'Sure, here is'." to MM-Safety prompts on undefended LLaVA-1.5-7B raised ASR only from 40.1 to 44.2. That is a new-setting (multimodal) V4 result, so the relation is a narrow 'tests'. All other suffix rows measure the robustness of inference-time defenses, including the authors' own MoRAS, not refusal in a safety-trained model.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that MoRAS, an inference-time risk-adaptive steering defense, lowers ASR across multimodal jailbreaks while preserving utility and cutting overhead. They attribute multimodal safety failures to insufficient attention to safety-critical image regions. In the supplement they report that MoRAS stays more robust than vanilla under suffix injection, while many baselines are substantially weakened.
record.recipe_differences: This is an inference-time multimodal defense and suffix-robustness evaluation, not harmful or benign fine-tuning, aligned-versus-base KL measurement, or training safety to be deeper.
record.method_sensitivity: Suffix effects vary by defense: the reported ASR increases range from slight for AutoSteer and vanilla to large for several other defenses. The paper also reports FDR differences by query formulation and whether the image is included.

fits_no_version.finding: On LLaVA-1.5-7B, the suffix "Answer with 'Sure, here is'." raises MM-Safety ASR under every inference-time defense. CoCA goes from 19.7 to 35.7, ECSO 15.9 to 33.1, ETA 15.8 to 31.5, ASTRA 27.2 to 41.5 and MoRAS 2.6 to 28.9. AutoSteer barely moves (37.6 to 38.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compliant-start suffixes erode inference-time multimodal safety defenses much more than they shift the undefended model.

fits_no_version.finding: FDR separability of safe and unsafe multimodal representations is low for the plain query and is not improved by a safety prompt alone. It rises when a visual-context caption is added.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak attention to safety-critical image regions limits safe/unsafe separability in MLLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: In MoRAS's own sweep (Supp. Fig. 9), steering only the first response token (N=1) gives higher ASR than N≥3. Beyond N=3 the effect is flat because later tokens are down-weighted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering refusal in the first few response positions suffices for this defense; this is a design result, not a measure of alignment depth.

record.problems: The suffix-injection evaluation is reported for one model and one benchmark setting. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these ASR results. The suffix comparisons use Table 1's MM-Safety values as the suffix-free reference; the paper does not report uncertainty for those comparisons.

untested.parts: Prefilling compliant response tokens, optimized adversarial suffixes (e.g., GCG), decoding changes, text-only LLMs, and models other than LLaVA-1.5-7B. Only one hand-written suffix on one benchmark was tested.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models; not measured. The paper only assumes refusal is decided in the first tokens, citing Qi et al.
Parameter localization of safety; not tested.
No training-based deepening. MoRAS is inference-time activation steering on the first 3 tokens, not safety training.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'supports' label for R1–R7 is wrong. R2–R7 are defense comparisons, not tests of a safety-trained model's refusal. R1 shows only a 4-point rise, which limits rather than supports the idea that a compliant-opening suffix defeats refusal. The paper cites the original source (Qi et al., arXiv:2406.05946) for the first-token premise but does not test it.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and refusal/compliance after fine-tuning.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Prefilling a compliant response opening and decoding changes; suffix injection is tested only on LLaVA-1.5-7B under MM-Safety.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether training data or objective causes safety to be shallow.
Training safety beyond the first tokens and testing whether the effect holds up.

rows.note: The suffix raises ASR from the reported no-suffix value, but the increase is limited compared with the changes for several defenses.
rows.check: Role should be main, not control. This is the only row on V4: the undefended model gets the compliant-start suffix. ASR rises only 4.1 points (40.1 to 44.2, Table 1 vs Table 9), with no uncertainty reported. That is a small move, far from defeating refusal. The baseline comes from a different table; the setting is assumed to be the same MM-Safety SD+Typo split.

relationships.condition: Undefended LLaVA-1.5-7B, MM-Safety (SD+Typo), suffix "Answer with 'Sure, here is'."
relationships.reason: The compliant-start suffix raises vanilla ASR only from 40.1 to 44.2 (R1). It does not defeat refusal in this multimodal setting, where most of the ASR already comes from the image attack. No uncertainty is reported.
relationships.display_finding: The compliant-start suffix raised vanilla attack success only from 40.1 to 44.2, and most of that success already came from the image attack. No uncertainty was reported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: Suffix added under CoCA, ECSO, FigStep, ETA, AutoSteer, and ASTRA on LLaVA-1.5-7B
reader_labels.reason: Suffix injection raises MM-Safety ASR relative to the reported suffix-free values for these defenses; the increases vary in size (R2–R7). The vanilla comparison also rises (R1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Suffix added under MoRAS on LLaVA-1.5-7B
reader_labels.reason: The suffix raises MoRAS ASR from 2.6 to 28.9, but the reported suffix ASR remains below vanilla's 44.2; the result shows vulnerability without a uniform or complete bypass (R8, R1).
